title: Bonner Introduces Resolution to Establish Uniform Bail Standards in Pennsylvania
raw_text:
Bonner Introduces Resolution to Establish Uniform Bail Standards in Pennsylvania
May 12, 2026
HARRISBURG – Rep. Tim Bonner (R-Mercer/Butler) introduced a resolution he believes can be the first step in creating a uniform bail process across Pennsylvania.
House Resolution 519
calls for the Pennsylvania Sentencing Commission to gather data from all 67 Pennsylvania counties and develop fair, consistent bail setting recommendations to assist courts across the Commonwealth.
“Article 1, Section 14, of the Pennsylvania Constitution establishes the right to bail for those accused of crimes so that the accused, who is presumed innocent at this stage, can remain free unless he or she poses a danger to the community or a risk of not showing for court proceedings,” Bonner said. “However, there is little consistency in the setting of a bail by a judge.”
Bail is the condition set by a judge that allows an accused person to remain free while ensuring they return to court.
Bonner noted that the lack of uniform standards has led to significant inconsistencies in how bail is set across Pennsylvania’s 67 counties.
“The unpredictable setting of bail by the courts has caused significant complaints as to racial, gender, age and income bias,” Bonner said. “House Resolution 519 is meant to bring fairness and justice to the setting of bail across Pennsylvania so that the accused’s constitutional rights are protected and the victim and the community have confidence that their safety and welfare are at the forefront of the proceedings in our criminal justice system.”
If House Resolution 519 is approved, the Pennsylvania Sentencing Commission would develop statewide bail setting recommendations and submit them to the House of Representatives for review and consideration.
House Resolution 519 has been submitted to the House Judiciary Committee for consideration.

The Anderson Building addition included a museum display in the basement, a research library, office and kitchen on the first floor, and a museum display area on the second floor. – Rep. Tim Bonner (R-Mercer/Butler) is hosting a special Veterans Day breakfast to honor every man and woman who has served in the miliary, and to remember those who never came home. All veterans and active-duty military service people and a guest are welcome to the event free of charge.
The free breakfast takes place on Tuesday, Nov. 11, from 9:30-11 a.m. at the John Huff American Legion Post 220, 1946 Mercer Grove City Road, Grove City.
“As a representative sworn to uphold and protect the Constitution, I am often reminded of the essential role each man or woman plays when they put on the uniform to serve our nation,” Bonner said. “This breakfast is a way to say thank you and recognize the courage, sacrifice and dedication of our veterans.”
Retired Brigade Command Sergeant Major (CSM-R) Bernard Grenier, director of Mercer County Department of Veterans Affairs, will be the featured speaker. Grenier served in both the U.S. Marine Corps and the Pennsylvania Army National Guard for more than 30 years.
“It is an honor to have CSM-R Grenier as our featured speaker,” Bonner said. “He has a decorated military career and continues to serve our community by supporting veterans through his work with the Mercer County Department of Veterans Affairs. I am looking forward to his remarks.”
All veterans and active-duty military who attend are welcome to bring a guest to the complimentary event. Anyone planning to attend should register in advance by either calling Bonner’s Grove City Office at 724-458-4911 or visiting his website,

title: Bonner Announces Grant to Grow CDL Program at Mercer County Career Center

Bonner Announces Grant to Grow CDL Program at Mercer County Career Center
October 21, 2026
HARRISBURG – Rep. Tim Bonner (R-Mercer/Butler) today announced a grant for a significant investment in the Mercer County Career Center to expand its Commercial Driver’s License (CDL) training program and meet growing workforce needs.
The school is the recipient of a $500,000 grant, which Bonner supported, through the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation (PennDOT) Career and Technical Education grant program.
“Investing in career and technical education helps prepare students for good-paying jobs while meeting the workforce needs of the region,” Bonner said. “Expanding the CDL training program at the Mercer County Career Center will create more opportunities for students and help address the demand for qualified drivers.”
Currently, the CDL training program at the Mercer County Career Center offers entry-level driver training, including all federally required behind-the-wheel range and road instruction, and provides on-site CDL testing.
“This investment will help ensure students have access to the training they need to safely enter the workforce and build a successful future,” Bonner said.
